title: Optimizing Treatment in Female Urgency Urinary Incontinence: Predictive Urodynamic Parameters for Conservative versus Botulinum Toxin Therapy
summary: This study aims to investigate whether urodynamic measurements in women with urgency urinary incontinence can serve as predictive factors for treatment selection. The goal is to identify patients who are unlikely to respond to conservative therapy early on, so they can be offered an alternative treatment with botulinum toxin sooner. This approach intends to improve treatment efficiency and reduce the overall duration of therapy.

interventions.name: Female patients with urgency or mixed urinary incontinence who, at the time of data collection, had undergone conservative pharmacological treatment and had not received any botulinum toxin therapy.
Female patients with urgency or mixed urinary incontinence who received botulinum toxin therapy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
female, ≥ 18 years, diagnosed with urge incontinence or mixed incontinence, has undergone urodynamic testing, has received pharmacological therapy and/or botulinum toxin injections into the bladder
Exclusion criteria:
Known urological pre-existing conditions such as bladder carcinoma, urethral stricture, bladder stones;
spinal cord syndrome
